issues.legal_issue: A dispute arising from a private occupancy agreement made before the owner became a member of a cooperative society is not referable to the society’s dispute-resolution process merely because the owner later became a member.
material_facts: The owner entered into an agreement permitting another person to occupy a flat before the cooperative society existed and before the owner became a member.
The occupant later sought fixation of standard rent, and the owner disputed the landlord-tenant relationship and sought referral of the dispute to the cooperative society’s registrar.
The owner entered into the occupancy agreement in a private capacity, not as a member dealing with the society.
issues.conclusion: The dispute did not fall within Section 91 of the Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Act, 1960, and was not referable to the Registrar for resolution under that section.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 91(1)(b) of the Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Act, 1960, a person claiming through a member must claim through a transaction or dealing that the member entered into with the society as a member. A dispute arising from a transaction the owner entered into in a private capacity does not fall within that provision. The Court applied Deccan Merchants Co-operative Bank Ltd. v. Dalichand Jugraj Jain, which held that a dispute arising from a member’s lease of the member’s own flat was outside Section 91 where the member had not acted as a member in entering into the lease.

rule.if: cooperative_dispute_referral and agreement_predates_membership and society_not_yet_formed and owner_acted_in_private_capacity

predicates.cooperative_dispute_referral: A party sought to have the dispute referred to a cooperative society’s dispute-resolution authority.
predicates.agreement_predates_membership: The owner entered into the agreement underlying the dispute before becoming a member of the society.
predicates.society_not_yet_formed: The society had not been formed when the owner entered into the agreement underlying the dispute.
predicates.owner_acted_in_private_capacity: The owner entered into the agreement underlying the dispute privately, rather than in a transaction or dealing with the society as a member.

issues.definition: When a dispute referral concerns an agreement made before the owner became a member, before the society existed, and in the owner’s private capacity, the dispute is not referable to the cooperative registrar.
